items.summary: नॉर्थ-ईस्ट दिल्ली यानि राजधानी का वो हिस्सा, जहां तंग गलियों और भीड़भाड़ के पीछे एक और दुनिया पल रही है. नाबालिगों का अंडरवर्ल्ड. यहां उम्र छोटी है, लेकिन हाथों में हथियार बड़े. यहां चाकू और कट्टों के साथ ये बच्चे सिर्फ डर नहीं बल्कि मौत भी बांट रहे हैं. कई महीनों तक हमने इस इलाके की खाक छानी. दिन हो या रात उन गलियों से लेकर उन ठिकानों तक पहुंचे. जहां से खौफ की ये कहानियां जन्म लेती हैं. हर वारदात के पीछे छिपे पैटर्न को समझने की कोशिश की और उन चेहरों तक पहुंचे जो इस अंडरवर्ल्ड का हिस्सा बन चुके हैं. दरअसल, यह उत्तर-पूर्वी दिल्ली की वो गलियां हैं, जिनके भीतर एक ऐसी दुनिया सांस लेती है, जिसे बहुत कम लोग करीब से देख पाते हैं. एक ऐसा अंधेरा संसार जहां कई नाबालिगों के हाथों तक किताबों से पहले हथियार पहुंच जाते हैं. यहां गैंग का हिस्सा बनना और अपराध की दुनिया में कदम रखना कई युवाओं के लिए असामान्य नहीं बल्कि एक कड़वी हकीकत बन चुका है. अक्सर, ये घटनाएं अखबार की सुर्खियां ही बनकर रह जाती हैं. आखिर ये बच्चे अपराध की दुनिया में क्यों बढ़ रहे हैं? क्या आसपास का माहौल इन्हें इस दिशा में ले जाता है? क्या गरीबी, बेरोजगारी और टूटता सामाजिक ढांचा इसकी बजह है? या फिर व्यवस्था इन्हें दूसरा रास्ता ही नहीं देती? अपराध की दुनिया का हिस्सा बन चुके ये बच्चे हमें बताते हैं कि ये खुला घूमते हैं, सिगरेट पीते हैं. हथियारों का शोक है. ये कहते हैं, "चाकू कट्टे-पिस्टल ये सब हमें हमारे ‘बड़े भाइयों’ से मिल जाता है." हालांकि, वे उन ‘बड़े भाइयों’ का नाम नहीं बताते हैं. हमने अपनी पड़ताल में पाया कि इनके पीछे कुछ बड़े गैंगस्टर काम करते हैं. इनमें कुछ जेल में हैं और कुछ जेल के बाहर हैं. वही इन्हें हथियार और बाकी असलहा भी इन्हीं लोगों से मिलते हैं. इसके बदले इन्हें कुछ सुविधाएं मुहैया कराई जाती हैं. इस बारे में हमने वर्तमान और पूर्व पुलिस अधिकारियों से बात की. नॉर्थ ईस्ट दिल्ली में करीब 14-15 सालों तक क्राइम ब्रांच और स्पेशल सेल का हिस्सा रहे विनय त्यागी कहते हैं कि दिल्ली पुलिस में जिसने जमना पार में नौकरी कर ली, उसने समझो पूरी दिल्ली में कर ली. वह इतना मैच्योर हो जाता है कि अपराधियों के काम करने का तरीका सब समझ लेता है. वहां छोटे से लेकर बड़े से बड़ा अपराध होता है. अपराध की दुनिया में एंट्री कैसे होती है? इस सवाल पर वह कहते हैं, “इन बच्चों को एक तो रुपये बहुत आसानी से मिल जाते हैं और जो बड़े-बड़े गैंगस्टर्स हैं या जो जेल में हैं. वो इन बच्चों का यूज करते हैं क्योंकि जुवेनाइल एक्ट में प्रावधान है कि तीन साल से ज्यादा की सजा नहीं है. चाहे मर्डर हो या रेप. बड़े-बड़े गैंग्स इन्हें हायर करते हैं. बच्चों को अपनी जरूरतें पूरी करनी होती हैं, उन्हें अपना टारगेट पूरा करना होता है.” इस डॉक्यूमेंट्री के लिए हमने इन बच्चों, पीड़ित परिवारों, पुलिस, साइकोलॉजिस्ट और क्रिमिनोलॉजिस्ट से बात की है. अपराध करने

items.title: Knives, pistols and ‘aura farming’: Inside Delhi’s teen ‘gangs’
items.summary: In the cramped, winding lanes of North-East Delhi, boys are picking up knives and country-made pistols before they ever pick up a schoolbook. Step behind the main roads here and you find a world of the underage offender. Armed with blades and homemade firearms, they don’t just spread fear, some of them deal in death. For months, we walked these lanes, day and night, tracking down the hideouts where these stories begin. We tried to trace the pattern behind each incident, and we sought out the young people who have become part of this world. Few outsiders ever see this side of North-East Delhi up close. For a striking number of young people here, drifting into a gang and into crime isn’t the exception, it's simply what happens. Most of the time, these stories surface only as a headline in the next day’s paper, then disappear. What draws children toward this life? Is it the neighbourhood they grow up in? Or is it that the system itself never gave them another road to take? The boys who are already part of this world talk about it almost casually, roaming the streets, and smoking. “We get our knives, our katta [country-made pistols], our pistols from our bade bhai [elder brothers],” they say, but they won’t give up their names. Our reporting found established gangsters, some behind bars, some still free, who supply the weapons and the ammunition and hand out small rewards in return to these underage offenders. Vinay Tyagi, who spent roughly 15 years in the Crime Branch and the Special Cell covering North-East Delhi, said, “Easy money is the first draw. The second is that the big players, whether they’re locked up or free, actively recruit minors, because the Juvenile Justice Act caps their maximum sentence at three years, no matter the charge. Larger gangs bring these boys in on purpose. And once they’re in, they have their own bills to pay and quotas to meet.” Watch the full video. Your support keeps news free. items.title: CJI Surya Kant says Collegium examining allegations by Justice Sandeep Mehta against Rajasthan acting CJ
items.summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Wednesday said that he has taken note of concerns raised by Supreme Court Justice Sandeep Mehta regarding Rajasthan High Court Acting Chief Justice SP Sharma. In a press statement issued on Wednesday evening, the CJI said that allegations against a sitting judge has to go through the established institutional process and a decision can be taken only after giving Justice Sharma an opportunity to respond to the allegations. The press statement was issued by the CJI after Bar & Bench reported on three letters written by Justice Mehta to the CJI seeking the transfer of Justice Sharma from Rajasthan over allegations including manipulation of case listings and misuse of office. Justice Mehta’s letters urged the Collegium to appoint a Chief Justice from another High Court to head the Rajasthan High Court with immediate effect. Justice Mehta accused Justice Sharma of manipulating case listings in favour of rich litigants and misusing his administrative powers ahead of his retirement, due later next month. In his August 2 letter, Justice Mehta referred to complaints allegedly made by judges of the Rajasthan High Court about Justice Sharma’s conduct. He also alleged that Justice Sharma had threatened fellow judges at the High Court with transfers by claiming proximity to the CJI. The letters cited two division bench orders of the Rajasthan High Court. In a batch of appeals over what Justice Mehta calls "priceless lands" in the city of Udaipur, the cases were listed before Justice Sharma's own bench at the Jaipur seat, despite an earlier judgment by Justice Sharma himself holding that such principal bench matters at Jodhpur seat could not be moved there. Another letter of August 17 alleged that a sitting Rajasthan High Court judge - Justice Uma Shankar Vyas - complained to fellow judges of vindictive conduct by Justice Sharma towards his wife, a senior district judiciary officer. The latest inspections covered 10 clubs, including the Bowring Club, Century Club, Karnataka State Cricket Association (KSCA) Club, Race Course Club, Catholic Club, Badminton Club, Tennis Club, Vijayanagara Club, Mahalakshmi Layout Club and Malleshwaram Club. At the KSCA Club, which operates a canteen at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium, inspectors found expired fish and other food products being stored on the premises. A stock of toor dal did not have details such as the packing date, batch number and maximum retail price. The inspection also flagged hygiene and food-handling practices at the club. Officials found that food handlers were not maintaining adequate personal hygiene and that vegetarian and non-vegetarian food was not being stored separately. Tilapia fish was also found without the required label details. The kitchen had plastic cutting boards, while the drainage system was blocked and the frozen-storage area was found to be unhygienic. Officials also reported that the utensils-cleaning area lacked adequate hygiene and that hot water was not available. The canteen was issued a notice following the inspection. Another notice was issued to the Mahalakshmi Layout Club over deficiencies in kitchen hygiene. Officials also found several food products that were either expired or did not meet labelling requirements, including packets of mixture and pani puri. At the Bowring Club, inspectors reportedly found cockroaches on the floor and in and around food containers and cartons. The inspections are part of a wider food-safety crackdown across Bengaluru, with authorities stepping up checks at hotels, restaurants, clubs and other establishments following a series of violations. In a recent three-day drive, food safety officials inspected 60 hotels and collected 77 food samples. They seized 640 kg of meat and 276 kg of rotten vegetables, besides other expired or unsafe food products. The crackdown also extended to premium restaurants and pubs. At Skyye Lounge in UB City, officials found 45 kg of rotten chicken and beef, including fungus-infested meat, along with vegetable cutlets and used cooking oil. items.title: Father, son die after inhaling toxic gas while cleaning well in Chennai
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A 55-year-old man and his 25-year-old son died of asphyxiation on Wednesday, August 26, after inhaling toxic gas while cleaning a well at a house near Sowcarpet in Chennai. The deceased were identified as Ravi, and his son Ayyanar, both natives of Tiruvannamalai district, who were residing at Chinnadurai Madam near Kodungaiyur in Chennai. According to the police, the duo had been engaged by Prashanth, a businessman and resident of Sowcarpet, to clean and remove slit from a well at his house on Ela Kandappan street. Ravi first climbed down into the well using a ladder and began clearing the silt. While working inside, he inhaled the toxic gas, lost consciousness and fell into the water. On seeing his father collapse, Ayyanar climbed down into the well in an attempt to rescue him. He too inhaled the gas and collapsed. Upon receiving information, a team from the Tamil Nadu Fire and Rescue Services reached the spot and entered the well using breathing apparatus and protective masks. They rescued both men from the well and shifted them to Rajiv Gandhi Government General Hospital. However, doctors examined them and declared them dead. Their bodies were sent for post-mortem examination. Elephant Gate police have registered a case under Section 106(1) (causing death by negligence) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and are investigating the circumstances leading to the deaths. When TNM asked the Elephant Gate police whether the duo had been provided safety kits while cleaning the well, police said it was unclear and that the investigation is ongoing.

items.title: Akash’s Dalit identity known to cops who tortured and killed him, finds CB-CID
items.summary: The CB-CID chargesheet in the custodial death of 26-year-old Dalit youth Akash Delison says the six policemen accused in his death knew that he belonged to the Scheduled Caste (SC) Devendrakula Vellalar community and assaulted him with the intention of causing his death. All six have been charged with offences under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, along with provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Akash, from Sivaganga district, died on March 8 while under treatment at the Government Rajaji Hospital (GRH) in Madurai, two days after his arrest by the Manamadurai police. Police had arrested Akash and another man, Guna, on March 6, in connection with an attempted murder case. Even though the chargesheet on Akash’s custodial torture and murder was filed before the III Additional District Judge for Protection of Civil Rights (PCR) cases in Madurai on June 18, Akash’s parents received a copy only recently. It names Inspector Dileepan, Sub-Inspector K Guhan, Grade-I Constable S Kaleeswaran, driver constable P Mahendran, constable L Deivendran, and constable B Palaniyappan as accused. The CB-CID has charged all six under section 3(2)(v) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, which applies when a person who is not a member of an SC or ST community commits an offence against an SC/ST person knowing their caste or tribal identity, along with the charges of murder and causing disappearance of evidence or giving false information to screen an offender. Dileepan, the first accused, has additionally been charged with knowingly recording or framing an incorrect document or electronic record as a public servant, with the intention of causing injury to another person. The caste identities of both the victim and the accused have been specifically recorded in the chargesheet. Akash is identified as belonging to the Hindu Devendrakula Vellalar community, which comes under the SC category. The chargesheet says Dileepan belongs to the Hindu Piramalai Kallar community, which is classified as Other Backward Class (OBC), and, in specified districts including Sivaganga, also as a Denotified (DNT) community. Guhan belonged to the Hindu Kallar community. Kaleeswaran belonged to the Hindu Tuluva Vellalar community. Mahendran belonged to the Hindu Gounder community and Deivendran and Palaniyappan to the Hindu Agamudayar community.
